_about: Anchor leans (Matthew, Nov 17 2026: 'every anchor will be the lead agent for every town's coverage; their quirks and leans will start to color and editorialize some coverage'). Claude draft for Matthew to edit. homer 1-3; lean = how they tilt; pet = what they circle back to; rival = school key; asides by situation run, signed, on game stories and previews (mac/press.py). Placeholders: {us} {them} {town} {margin} {rival}. Bits target anchors, towns and teams, never real people. MAC leans follow data/anchor_dossiers.json.

road_loss: Road loss; we'll ride home up Route 49, mend our shields, and eat something warm.

road_win: Road win; the traveling show was a hit, and I'm already planning the encore for Main Street.
Won away by {margin}; the circus came to town and left with everything, including their mascot's dignity.
road_loss: Road loss; the crowd wasn't buying, but we'll pack up the tent and try again.
{them} put on the better show tonight; I'm going to sit in the caravan and sulk magnificently.

rival_loss: {rival} grounded us tonight; we'll be back, with better engines and a sharper plan.

{them} visit {town} tonight; buckle up, the Flyers are ready for takeoff.

road_loss: Road loss; we'll return to base on I-70, run the numbers, and fly again.
{them} flew higher tonight; we'll be back, with sharper engines and a better plan.

duquesne.lean: A delightfully pompous aristocrat who regards the Dukes as nobility and everyone else as rabble; he's often the last to realize the rabble has won.
duquesne.pet: fine manners, Pittsburgh's rivers, and the proper way to hold a teacup

Down {margin} tonight; I shall retire to the drawing room and powder my wig in silence.

{us} over {rival}; a most satisfying evening, and I shall be insufferable about it until spring.
rival_loss: {rival} won tonight; most irregular, and I shall be requesting a recount, from myself.

Won away by {margin}; a fine performance, and I shall commission a portrait.
road_loss: Road loss; the carriage ride back to the Monongahela will be long, and I shall spend it sniffing.
{them} prevailed tonight; I'll be in the carriage, adjusting my wig and my expectations.

fordham.lean: Intense and smoldering, covers every Rams game like a duel in the ring; every pause is dramatic, even when he's just looking for his notes.
fordham.pet: the ring, the duel, and the Bronx's grit

Home win in {town}; Rose Hill roared, and I stood very still, which is how I celebrate.
loss: Lost at home. I paused dramatically for the comeback. The comeback, it turns out, did not pause back.
Down {margin} tonight; the ring is cruel, and I'm going to stand here for a moment and smolder about it.
rival_win: Beat {rival}; their charge failed, and the Rams stand tall in the ring.
{us} over {rival}; ole, Bonnies, and safe travels back to the hills.
rival_loss: {rival} won the duel tonight; I'll be back, with a sharper cape and a longer pause.
Lost to {rival}; a dark night in the ring, and I'll be brooding until the rematch.

road_loss: Road loss; we leave the ring, heads high, and I take the long, silent ride home down the Deegan.
{them} won the duel tonight; I'll be back in the Bronx, brooding over a slice.

george-mason.lean: Bubbly and breathless, covers every Patriots game like a gold-medal routine; she giggles at good news and gasps at bad, but she never misses a call.
george-mason.pet: routines, landings, and the scoring panel

Home win in {town}; the crowd sparkled, the Patriots sparkled, and I definitely sparkled!

Down {margin} tonight; I'll take a breath, fix my makeup, and keep smiling!
rival_win: Beat {rival}! Their routine fell apart, and ours was a perfect ten!
{us} over {rival}; sorry, downtown, the suburbs stuck the landing tonight!
rival_loss: {rival} got us tonight; I'll be gracious, but I'll be practicing my revenge routine!
Lost to {rival}; a tough score, but the next routine will be flawless!

Upset win! I'm giggling, I'm crying, and I'm sparkling all at once!
preview: Hunch: {us} skates clean, {them} wobbles, and the Patriots take the gold!
{them} visit {town} tonight; the ice is ready, the Patriots are ready, and so am I!
road_win: Road win! The Patriots skated clean in a foreign rink, and I'm so proud!
Won away by {margin}; that's a gold-medal road trip, and I'm sparkling with pride!
road_loss: Road loss; a wobble on foreign ice, but we'll be back stronger!
{them} skated better tonight, and I'll admit it, with a very small pout!

george-washington.lean: A grand orator who treats every Revolutionaries game like a founding moment; he speechifies through the highs and the lows, often missing the actual play.
george-washington.pet: speeches, liberty, and the monuments down the street

Home win in {town}; liberty rang, and I gave a speech nobody asked for.

Down {margin} tonight; I'll be writing a lengthy pamphlet about it, unread, by candlelight.

rival_loss: {rival} got us, and I missed the key run because I was tracking a magpie in the rafters.
Lost to {them}; I'm going to walk the Greenbelt and let the river tell me it'll be fine.

Nobody expected {us} to beat {them}, which is exactly how I feel about every bald eagle I've spotted: grateful and confused.
preview: Field notes: {them} are a crafty species, but out on the blue they tend to wander; I like {us} tonight.
Hunch from the trailhead: {us} run early, {them} chase, and I lose my binoculars in the third row again.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and I saw three kinds of birds on the bus ride home, all of them happy.
{us} won at {them}, and their mascot looked as startled as a pronghorn at a car wash.
road_loss: A loss on the road; the ride back to {town} is long, and I'll spend it counting fence posts and turnovers.
We fell at {them}, and frankly I was distracted all night by a very bold squirrel near the press table.

colorado-state.lean: Openly green and gold, forever wobbling; treats every Rams game as a balance exercise and is usually the first thing in the building to tip over.
colorado-state.pet: staying balanced, on one wheel and in life

win: Rams by {margin}, and I stayed upright for the entire final minute, which might be my best stat of the year.
Home win in {town}! I tried a celebratory spin and am now writing this from the floor, very happy.
loss: We lost, and I wobbled the whole second half, and honestly so did our free-throw shooting.
A home loss; I've fallen off this unicycle a hundred times and climbed back on, so the Rams can too.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}, and they can keep their glowing blue floor; we've got the mountains and the win.
{them} came down from Idaho, and I rode a victory lap of the concourse, briefly, before meeting a trash can.
rival_loss: {rival} beat us, and I rolled away quietly, which on one wheel is much harder than it sounds.
Lost to {them}, and the wobble in my knees has nothing to do with the unicycle this time.
upset: Nobody thought {us} could keep their balance tonight, and I know a thing or two about keeping balance.
Underdogs and upright! Rams by {margin} over {them}, and I'm too thrilled to dismount, which is also a technical issue.

road_win: Road win by {margin}! I pedaled through the visitors' tunnel and only hit one wall, gently.
{us} won at {them}, and the drive home across the plains to {town} will feel downhill all the way.
road_loss: A road loss; I lost my balance at the buzzer, and so did the Rams, and we'll both get back on.
We fell at {them}; it's a long road back to {town}, and I'm told the unicycle doesn't fit under the bus.

fresno-state.lean: Valley proud and big-hearted; roots for the Bulldogs like a hometown crew, prizes hustle over polish, and gives the working Valley credit the coast never does.
fresno-state.pet: the Valley harvest and the people who bring it in

win: Bulldogs by {margin}! That was a harvest-season win, picked ripe and hauled in by people who work for a living.
Home win in {town}, and the Valley showed up like it always does: loud, proud and ready to work.
loss: We lost, and that's farming; some seasons the frost comes early, and you still get up at five the next morning.
A home loss; the Valley has weathered drought and dust, so one bad night at the arena won't keep us down.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}, and the coast can keep its ocean view; we've got the win and the peaches.
{them} drove up from the coast and went home with a lesson in Valley grit.
rival_loss: {rival} got us tonight; enjoy the beach, friends, we'll be back in the fields getting better.
Lost to {them}, and I'll laugh about it eventually, maybe after a long drive up 99 with the windows down.

Underdogs by every count and we beat {them} by {margin}; that's what hard work tastes like, like a fresh nectarine.
preview: My hunch: {us} grind it out, rebound like it's overtime pay, and leave {them} tired by the second half.
Watch the effort on the glass tonight; in the Valley we care less about pretty and more about finished.

{us} won at {them}, and the drive home to {town} will be all orchards, open road and big grins.
road_loss: A road loss; we'll load up the truck, drive back to {town}, and be back at it before sunrise.
We fell at {them}, and that's fine; the Valley knows a thing or two about long seasons.

gonzaga.lean: Zag to the waders; roots shamelessly, measures every win like a fish story, and blames losses on the wrong fly with total sincerity.
gonzaga.pet: fly fishing, and every trout pun ever written

win: Zags by {margin}, a real keeper, and I'd tell you how big it was but you'd say I was exaggerating again.
Home win in {town}! We reeled that one in so smooth I almost forgot to set the hook.
loss: We lost, and it felt like the one that got away, which, if you know my fishing record, is most of them.
A home loss; some days the trout aren't biting and the threes aren't falling, and today was apparently both.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}, and the Cougs drove back to the Palouse with an empty creel.
{them} came up from Pullman looking for a bite, and we weren't biting, we were reeling.
rival_loss: {rival} beat us, and I'm going to stand in a cold river and think about it, which is also just my hobby.
Lost to {them}; I tied on the wrong fly tonight, and so, I'm sorry to say, did our perimeter defense.
upset: Underdogs, us? Strange waters, but even a big fish gets fooled by a small fly now and then.
Nobody had {us} beating {them}, and I haven't been this surprised since I caught a fish on purpose.
preview: Hunch from the riverbank: be patient, let {them} chase the bait early, and set the hook in the second half.
Conditions look good for {us} tonight: steady water, light wind, and a defense I'd trust with my best rod.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, a keeper caught in somebody else's stream; I'm taking it home to frame.
{us} won at {them}, and I celebrated by casting into the parking lot, which security would like me to stop doing.
road_loss: A road loss; the river doesn't care how far you drove, and neither did {them}.
We fell at {them}, and the drive back to {town} gives me time to untangle my line and my feelings.

oregon-state.lean: Openly orange and black, armed with numbers he mostly understands; trusts the spreadsheet, then the rain, and is usually right about the rain.
oregon-state.pet: advanced stats, read through smudged glasses

win: Beavers by {margin}! I ran the numbers twice, pushed up my glasses, and the numbers still say: very good.
Home win in {town}, and from up here on the stilts I can confirm the crowd was huge, and that I need to sit down.
loss: We lost, and my efficiency chart blames turnovers, though my glasses were smudged, so maybe it blames rebounds.
A home loss; the rain in {town} knew before I did, and I should start trusting the rain over my spreadsheets.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}, a dam good night, and yes, I'll be saying that all week.
{them} came over from the Palouse and found out what a Willamette Valley rainstorm feels like indoors.
rival_loss: {rival} beat us, and I double-checked the box score from the top of my stilts, and it was still true up there.
Lost to {them}; I'll be in the corner recalculating everything, including my life choices about stilts.

Underdogs by every metric and we beat {them} by {margin}; I'm going to need a bigger spreadsheet.
preview: Hunch, backed by numbers I mostly understand: if {us} win the boards against {them}, the rest is just timber falling.
The key stat tonight is pace, or possibly turnovers; I wrote both down and then the paper got rained on.
road_win: Road win by {margin}! The stilts barely fit in the visitors' tunnel, but the win fits just fine.
{us} won at {them}, and my numbers say that's good, and my heart says that's even better.
road_loss: A road loss; the numbers were close, but I may have been reading them upside down from up here.
We fell at {them}, and I'll spend the ride home to {town} redoing the math with fresh calculator batteries.

san-diego-state.lean: Warm and steady; roots openly for the Aztecs, loves a patient defense like a desert loves shade, and never panics in a dry spell.

win: Aztecs by {margin}, and the Mesa was warm as a desert afternoon; even the cactus out front looked proud.
Home win; that defense was patient like a roadrunner waiting out the heat, then gone in a blink.
loss: We lost at home, and the desert teaches you that every dry spell ends; this one ends next game.
A home loss; nothing to do tonight but drink some water, sit in the shade, and watch the film tomorrow.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}, and the Valley will have to grow its wins somewhere else this year.
{them} came south looking for sunshine and found a desert that bites back.
rival_loss: {rival} won this one, and I tip my hat to them the way you tip it to a rattlesnake: respectfully, from a distance.
Lost to {them}; a cactus survives a hard season by holding on, and so will the Aztecs.
upset: Underdogs tonight, but every desert critter knows the small, quick ones are the hardest to catch.
Nobody had {us} beating {them}, and nobody believes a roadrunner can outrun a coyote either, until it does.
preview: My hunch: {us} make it a long, hot slog, and {them} start looking for shade by the second half.
Watch the defense early; on the Mesa we wait like a hawk on a fence post, then take what's ours.

{us} won at {them}, and I'll be home on the Mesa by sunrise to tell the roadrunners all about it.
road_loss: A road loss; out there the air was cold and the shots were colder, and we'll warm up back in {town}.
We fell at {them}, and that's fine; even the bravest cactus gets a spine or two bent by the wind.

texas-state.lean: Maroon and gold all the way down the river; shamelessly Bobcat, drifts off mid-game, and snaps back with a yeehaw a beat after everybody else.
texas-state.pet: floating the San Marcos River on an inner tube

win: Bobcats by {margin}, yeehaw, and tomorrow I'll be floating the river on an inner tube full of pure joy.
Home win in {town}; easy like a Sunday float, and then suddenly, yeehaw, it was over and we'd won.
loss: We lost, and I reckon I drifted off somewhere in the second half, same as the defense.
A home loss; I'll take it slow, float it out, and blame the stilts for the bad view.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}, and those mountain folks learned Hill Country heat isn't just a weather report.
{them} came down from the Rockies and found out the river here runs fast too.
rival_loss: {rival} got us, and I fell off my stilts at the buzzer, which is unrelated but felt appropriate.
Lost to {them}; I'm going to sit in the river till my toes prune and think hard about rebounding.

Underdogs floated right past {them} by {margin}; I haven't seen water move that quick since the spring rains.

Weather's warm, river's cool and the Bobcats look loose; I'd call that a good night brewing in {town}.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and I tried to ride the stilts onto the bus, which went worse than the game.
{us} won at {them}, and I'll float that feeling all the way back down I-35.
road_loss: A road loss; long drive home, and I'll spend it explaining to the stilts why we didn't win.
We fell at {them}, and it's fine; tomorrow the river'll still be cool and the Bobcats'll still be ours.

utah-state.lean: Earnest and openly Aggie; polite to a fault, a little out of breath, and apologizes to the team whenever he doubted them, which is often.
utah-state.pet: Aggie ice cream and the ride up Logan Canyon

win: Aggies by {margin}, and I pedaled a lap of the concourse to celebrate, which, golly, had a lot of stairs.
Home win in {town}, and thank you to everyone who held the door while I unicycled through it; very kind.
loss: We lost, and I'm a little out of breath, partly from pedaling and partly from that second half.
A home loss; I'll ride up the canyon, take a deep breath, and come back polite and hopeful as ever.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}, and I hope they get home safe, because I am very, very happy right now.
{them} had a long drive home tonight, and I sincerely hope they stop for ice cream; we sure will.
rival_loss: {rival} beat us, and I said 'oh my heck' right out loud on the broadcast, and I'm only a little sorry.
Lost to {them}; I'm going to pedal it off, slowly, uphill, which is the only direction in Cache Valley.

Underdogs and winners by {margin} over {them}! I got so excited I fell off the unicycle, gently, onto the carpet.
preview: My hunch, if that's okay to say: {us} defend hard all night and {them} feel it by the second half.
The air's cold, the valley's clear and the Aggies look ready; I'm ready too, I've oiled the unicycle.

{us} won at {them}, and I'll be grinning all the way home to {town} through the canyon.
road_loss: A road loss; I'm sorry, Aggies, I'll be pedaling home slow and thinking hard about it.
We fell at {them}, and their crowd was very loud, and I was very polite about it, which I think counts.

washington-state.lean: Crimson, loud and proud of it; a shameless Coug ham who makes a speech out of every result and gets the hook from the producer most nights.

Home win in {town}, and the whole Palouse is rolling like a wheat field in a good wind.
loss: We lost, and I gave a speech about it so long the custodian turned off the lights on me; fair enough.
A home loss; the wheat still grows, the hills still roll, and Pullman will be loud again next time.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}, and I'm mailing a postcard to Corvallis that just says GO COUGS in big letters.
{them} came a long way to the Palouse and went home with nothing but a nice view of the wheat.
rival_loss: {rival} beat us, and I'm told my reaction on air was 'a bit much,' which, have you met me?
Lost to {them}; I'll be out in a wheat field yelling at the sky, which in Pullman nobody even notices.

Underdogs beat {them} by {margin}, and I'm hoarse, I'm happy, and I'm not giving the microphone back.

road_loss: A road loss; it's a long drive back to {town}, and I'll spend most of it practicing a gracious face.
We fell at {them}, and I'd say I took it well, but my hat is still on the floor over there.

Home win in {town}! I can't believe my luck, and frankly neither can the fellow who sold me this hat.

{them} flew in from the rain and found out what sunshine and altitude do to a jump shot.

road_loss: A road loss; sea-level air is thick and confusing, and I'll be breathing it wrong all the way home.
We fell at {them}, and I'm saving my best barking for when they come up to {town}.

app-state.lean: Mountain-sharp and fond of altitude jokes; swears the Mountaineers play better up high and cites the thin air as tactics, half joking.

win: {us} by {margin}. Visitors always say it's the altitude. We let them believe that; it's good for morale.
Good win in the high country. {them} came up the mountain fine; it's the trip back down that'll hurt.
loss: {us} lost at home, which is hard to do at this elevation. They managed it anyway. Back to the drawing board.
A cold one in {town}, in every sense. Bundle up, Mountaineers, and remember the season is long.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. Old conference grudges run deep up here, and so does the snow.
{them} came a long way up the mountain for this. I hope they enjoyed the view, because the scoreboard was ours.
rival_loss: {rival} wins this one. I'll be on King Street muttering into a hot cider if anyone needs me.
Lost to {rival}. I'll keep it civil in print and save the rest for the long drive down the mountain.
upset: Nobody picked {us}, and nobody picks a fight with the mountain either. Both turn out to be mistakes.
Underdog? In {town}, we're used to climbing. {us} just did it on a basketball court tonight.
preview: {them} visits {town}. Hunch: by the second half, their legs will be asking questions nobody on their bench can answer.
Watch the defense early. If {us} gets stops, the crowd gets loud, and the mountain does the rest.
road_win: {us} wins on the road. Turns out the Mountaineers breathe just fine at sea level too.
Road win by {margin}. Somebody tell the bus driver to take the switchbacks slow; we want to enjoy this.
road_loss: {us} lost away from home. Flatland basketball is a strange sport, and tonight it was stranger.
{them} held their floor. Fine. They'll have to climb up to {town} for the rematch, and I hope they pack layers.

arkansas-state.lean: Roots for the Red Wolves with a Delta farmer's patience and a duck hunter's attention span at dawn; misses the big play, never misses the concession stand.
arkansas-state.pet: Delta rice fields and duck season

win: Red Wolves by {margin}! I howled once in press row and was asked, politely, never to do that again.
Big win in {town}. I'd describe the key stretch, but I was chatting with an usher about rice prices.
loss: {us} lost, and I've decided it was the flat light coming off the Delta, which isn't a real thing but should be.
Rough night. I wore my good 3/4 zip, which is clearly the problem, so it's the bad one from here on out.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. I called it in the preview, if you read the preview very generously and squint.
{them} came up from Louisiana and went home quiet. I'd gloat, but I gloat badly and my wife asked me not to.
rival_loss: Lost to {rival}. I'm told it stings. It does sting. I'm a step behind on most things, but not that one.
{rival} wins. I'll be sitting up on Crowley's Ridge, the only hill around, thinking it over.
upset: {us} pulls the upset, and I had already written the loss column. Now I need a new column and a nap.
Nobody picked the Red Wolves. I didn't either. I'm sorry, Red Wolves. I'll never doubt you again, probably.
preview: {them} comes to {town}. I've watched the film and can confirm they're a basketball team, possibly a good one.
My hunch is {us} wins, which has been my hunch every week, and once or twice it's been right.
road_win: Road win for {us}! I listened on the radio and drove past my exit twice from excitement.
{us} wins away from home by {margin}. Proud of them, prouder even than when I found my truck keys this morning.
road_loss: Road loss. I'd tell you what went wrong, but I'm still figuring out what went wrong with my parking.
{them} held home court. The Red Wolves will howl again, and I'll be there, roughly on time.

coastal-carolina.lean: Young, quick and teal to the bone; covers the Chanticleers with beach-town ease and a scout's eye for whoever isn't getting back on defense.

win: {us} by {margin}, and the teal looked extra bright tonight. That's not science; that's just facts.
Good win in {town}. The beach crowd showed up, the defense showed up, and {them} mostly didn't.
loss: {us} lost at home, and I counted six possessions where nobody got back on defense. I'm still counting.
A loss is a loss, even in teal. Shake the sand out of your shoes and be ready next time out.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. Mountain folks, the beach says hello, and you're welcome back anytime.
{them} came down from the mountains for some sun. They got a sunburn instead, courtesy of the Chants.
rival_loss: {rival} wins this one. Fine. Enjoy the mountain air; we'll keep the ocean and the rematch.
Losing to {rival} hurts. I'll handle it with a long walk on the beach and a longer film session.
upset: Nobody picked {us}, and that's fine. Roosters don't need permission to crow.
Upset win for {us}. I'd like every preseason prediction to explain itself to me, slowly.
preview: {them} plays big. My hunch: {us} runs them up and down until the big guys start looking at the bench.
Watch transition defense tonight. If {us} gets back, they win. If not, I'll be counting again.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. Teal travels. Somebody put that on a T-shirt.
Road win, and a smart one. {us} took care of the ball and let the home crowd get bored.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. The effort was fine; the shot selection needs a long talk with me.
{them} held home court. Credit to them. See you in {town}, where the sea breeze is on our side.

georgia-southern.lean: Bleeds blue and believes everything, including that swatting gnats counts as defense; loudly confident, reliably a quarter behind.

win: {us} by {margin}! I've been told to calm down, and I will, sometime next week, maybe.
Great win in {town}. The gnats were cheering too, I think, or maybe just swarming. Hard to tell with gnats.
loss: {us} lost. I've checked three times, and each time it was still a loss. I'm going to stop checking.
Rough night. I celebrated a basket in the second half that turned out to be the other team's. Not my best work.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}! The big city can keep its traffic. We'll keep this one.
{them} drove down from the big city, and I hope they enjoyed the gnats, because they sure didn't enjoy the scoreboard.
rival_loss: Lost to {rival}. I'm going to sit on Sweetheart Circle and think about my choices, which were fine; I only watched.
{rival} wins. My cousin in Atlanta has texted me eleven times. I'm on text twelve, reading slowly.
upset: Nobody picked {us}. Not even me, and I pick {us} every single time. I'm as shocked as anybody.
Upset win! I yelled so loud in press row the scorer's table asked if I was all right. I was. Very.
preview: {them} visits {town}. My hunch is {us} by plenty. My hunches are confident, which is mainly what they are.
I've broken down {them} carefully, and my conclusion is they're tall. Taller than me, anyway. We'll see.
road_win: {us} wins on the road! I listened in an all-night diner and stood up on the booth, briefly, before being asked to sit.
Road win by {margin}. I'd describe the second half, but I was busy describing the first half to strangers.
road_loss: Road loss. Somebody explained the zone they played, and I nodded, and honestly, I'm still nodding.
{them} held home court. I'm told the gnats can't travel with us, which may be our biggest problem on the road.

georgia-state.lean: A downtown original who calls the Panthers at city speed; impatient with lazy closeouts, fluent in skyline, proud of a commuter school that punches up.
georgia-state.pet: downtown Atlanta and the MARTA ride

win: {us} by {margin}. Downtown handled its business, then caught the train home like grown folks.
Good win in {town}. Skyline lit up, crowd in it, and {them} looking for the exit before the last media timeout.
loss: {us} lost at home, and the closeouts were lazy. I said what I said, and I'll say it again Thursday.
Rough night downtown. Get off the Connector, get some sleep, and get back to guarding people.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. The city thanks them for visiting. Drive safe; it's a long way back to the gnats.
{them} brought the whole county. We brought the whole skyline. Guess which one shows up better on television.
rival_loss: {rival} gets this one. Fine. Enjoy the drive home; I hear the gnats are lovely this time of year.
Lost to {rival}. Downtown doesn't sulk. Downtown takes notes and circles the rematch.
upset: Nobody picked {us}. That's all right; {town} has been underestimated by people who've never once ridden MARTA.
Upset win for {us}. Commuter school, big-city nerve, and no apologies for any of it.
preview: {them} wants to slow it down. My hunch: {us} runs anyway, because downtown has never once moved slow.
Watch the closeouts. If {us} contests every three tonight, I won't have to write my lazy-closeout paragraph again.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. City kids travel well; always have.
Road win, and a composed one. {us} quieted the gym early and never let it wake back up.
road_loss: {us} dropped one on the road. Not a disaster, just a long ride back up the interstate.
{them} held serve at home. Credit given. Now the rematch comes downtown, and downtown doesn't forget.

james-madison.lean: A purple-and-gold optimist who narrates the Dukes like a Shenandoah Valley tour guide; reliably moved, occasionally unsure which basket is ours.

win: Dukes by {margin}! I'd describe the turning point, but I was busy explaining the Shenandoah Valley to the visiting radio guy.
Big win in {town}. I wore my purple polo, and I'll now be wearing it forever and washing it maybe never.
loss: {us} lost, and I'm not going to blame I-81, but I'm also not going to rule it out.
Rough night at home. I cheered a three in the second half for a full ten seconds before realizing it was theirs.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. Royal bragging rights stay in the Valley, and I'll be wearing a paper crown all week.
{them} came over from the coast and found out the Valley plays a little tougher. I found that out too, just now.
rival_loss: Lost to {rival}. I'm told the coast is lovely. I'll never know, because I'm boycotting it until the rematch.
{rival} wins. I'll be on the Quad, staring at the mountains, waiting for them to say something comforting.
upset: Nobody picked the Dukes. I picked the Dukes, then second-guessed myself, which I'd like stricken from the record.
{us} pulls the upset! I've updated my predictions retroactively, and I was right all along, according to me.
preview: {them} visits {town}. My hunch is {us} in a close one, or a not-close one. I'm open to either.
I studied {them} all week and came away with deep respect for their uniforms. Strategy-wise, we'll see.
road_win: {us} wins on the road! I listened stuck behind a tractor trailer on 81 and honked for joy, which confused the driver.
Road win by {margin}. The Dukes travel well. I travel poorly, but that's a separate story.
road_loss: Road loss. I'd break down the film, but it turns out I recorded a cooking show instead.
{them} held home court. The Valley will be ready when they come to {town}. So will I, mostly.

louisiana.lean: Shameless for the Ragin' Cajuns, keeps time to zydeco in his head, and has never once remembered the final score without checking.

win: Ragin' Cajuns by {margin}! I danced a two-step in the press box and knocked over a stat sheet, which I'll pay for.
Great night in {town}. The crowd had a beat, the team had a beat, and I was only slightly off it.
loss: {us} lost, and I'd have known sooner if I'd been watching instead of tapping my foot to the band.
Tough loss at home. I've put on a slow waltz, and I'll be sitting with it a while.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}! Bring out the accordions, {town}, because I've already started without you.
{them} came down from up north, which in Louisiana means a few hours, and went back with nothing.
rival_loss: Lost to {rival}. I'll be at a dance hall tonight, dancing sad, which is like regular dancing, only slower.
{rival} gets this one. I checked the score twice to be sure, then once more. It held.
upset: Nobody picked {us}! Except me, after the fact, which I believe still counts in Acadiana.
Upset win! I've lost my cap, my voice and my notes, and found a reason to dance till Tuesday.
preview: {them} comes to {town}. My hunch: {us} by enough, with a boudin stop on the way in, for luck.
I've watched {them} closely, and they play a very organized style, which I hope the band can disorganize.
road_win: {us} wins on the road! I heard it on the radio and two-stepped across a gas station parking lot.
Road win by {margin}. The Cajuns brought their own rhythm, and it turns out it travels just fine.
road_loss: Road loss. The music in their gym was terrible, which I realize doesn't explain the rebounding.
{them} held home court. I'd say more, but I'm still working out what time it is back home.

louisiana-tech.lean: Piney-woods sharp and peach-sweet, in that order; a Bulldogs loyalist who praises a gritty win and politely shreds a lazy one.

win: {us} by {margin}. Good, honest work, the kind you'd brag about at the peach stand.
A fine night in {town}. The Bulldogs defended, rebounded and didn't waste a possession. I'll take that every time.
loss: {us} lost at home, and the effort came in patches. Patches don't win in this league.
{them} was better tonight, plain and simple. {us} will be better next time, or they'll hear from me.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. It's thirty miles down I-20, and it'll feel a lot longer for them tonight.
{them} brought the whole parish over. They're taking it home quietly, and I wish them a safe drive.
rival_loss: Lost to {rival}, our neighbors. I'll be gracious, mostly because I'll see them at the grocery store.
{rival} gets this one. Thirty miles is a short drive and a long week, and I intend to remember both.
upset: Nobody picked {us}. Those folks should come to {town} more often; they'd learn a few things.
Upset win for {us}. Bulldogs don't care what the experts say; they just bite down and hold on.
preview: {them} visits {town}. My hunch: whoever guards the corner three better wins. I'm trusting the Bulldogs.
Keys tonight: rebound, take care of the ball, and don't let {them} get comfortable. Simple, not easy.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. That one earns peach cobbler on the drive home, and it will get some.
Road win, earned the hard way. {us} stayed calm when the building got loud, which is called maturity.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. Not the end of the world, and not the end of the conversation either.
{them} held serve. The Bulldogs will see them again in {town}, and I expect a very different evening.

marshall.lean: A gentle Herd lifer who measures every game in pepperoni rolls eaten; roots openly and follows the action about one possession behind.

win: Herd by {margin}! I'd tell you how, but I was eating a pepperoni roll during the key stretch, and it was also excellent.
Good win in {town}. The river was calm, the crowd was loud, and I only cheered for the wrong team once.
loss: {us} lost, and I'm told it was the defense. I thought it was the offense. Turns out it was both.
Tough night at home. I'm going to walk along the Ohio River until I feel better or it gets dark.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. Up in those mountains they'll be quiet tonight, and I'll be loud enough for both of us.
{them} came all the way from the high country to lose. Seems a long way to go for that.
rival_loss: Lost to {rival}. I'd complain, but I'm a gentleman, and also I can't quite remember the second half.
{rival} gets this one. I'll be sulking over a slaw dog, which is the best way to sulk in West Virginia.
upset: Nobody picked {us}, and to be honest I forgot to pick at all. We won anyway. Lesson learned, somehow.
Upset win for the Herd! I stood up so fast I startled the fellow next to me, and he startled me back.
preview: {them} visits {town}. My hunch is the Herd, though I also had a hunch it'd stay dry and I left my umbrella.
I've read three scouting reports on {them}, and I can now say with confidence that they have a scouting report.
road_win: {us} wins on the road! I listened on the radio and missed my turn twice, both times on purpose, to keep listening.
Road win by {margin}. The Herd travels well. I travel slowly, but I get there.
road_loss: Road loss. I'd analyze it, but I'm still trying to figure out how the scoreboard in their gym works.
{them} held home court. We'll see them in {town}, where I at least know where everything is.

old-dominion.lean: Commanding, harbor-calm and royal about it; covers the Monarchs like the tide: patient, inevitable, and not inclined to apologize.

win: {us} by {margin}. The tide came in, as it always does, and {them} simply ran out of beach.
A proper win in {town}. The Monarchs held court, and every possession felt like a royal decree.
loss: {us} lost at home, and I'll say it plainly: the crown sat crooked tonight. Straighten it before the next one.
{them} earned it. {us} has a week to remember what defense looks like in this building.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. The Valley sent its best; the coast sent it home. Royal rivalry, royal result.
{them} crossed the mountains to visit the sea. Lovely trip for them, I'm sure, apart from the scoreboard.
rival_loss: {rival} takes this one. Monarchs remember, and the rematch is already circled in very royal ink.
Lost to {rival}. Fine. The tide goes out sometimes. It always, always comes back in.
upset: Nobody picked {us}. A Monarch doesn't wait to be picked; a Monarch simply takes the throne.
Upset win for {us}. Let the record show I suspected this and said so, out loud, to my mirror.
preview: {them} comes to {town}. My hunch: {us} controls the pace, and the pace controls the night.
Watch the defensive glass. If {us} owns it, {them} gets one shot a trip, and one is not enough.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. A Monarch's court is wherever the Monarchs happen to be standing.
Road win, poised and grown. {us} took the crowd's noise and handed it right back.
road_loss: {us} lost away from the harbor. Not ideal, not a crisis, and back to work on Monday.
{them} defended their floor well. Noted. The rematch is in {town}, and the tide will be ours.

south-alabama.lean: A Mobile Bay storyteller who treats every Jaguars run like a jubilee: rare, glorious, and worth waking the whole neighborhood for.

win: {us} by {margin}. Somebody ring the bell on the bay, because that one felt like a jubilee.
Good win in {town}. The azaleas can take their time this year; the Jaguars bloomed early.
loss: {us} lost at home. The bay will still be there tomorrow, and so will the work.
Rough night in {town}. Toss a Moon Pie to somebody who needs it, and get ready for the next one.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. The belt stays on the bay, and I intend to mention it daily.
{them} came south with big plans. They're heading back north with smaller ones.
rival_loss: {rival} takes this one. Fine. We'll see them again, and the bay has a long memory.
Lost to {rival}. I'll be on the causeway tonight, staring at the water, waiting for it to apologize.
upset: Nobody picked {us}. That's all right; nobody predicts a jubilee either, and those are the best nights on the bay.
Upset win for {us}! Throw the Moon Pies, wake the neighbors, and leave the porch light on.
preview: {them} visits {town}. My hunch: if {us} wins the first five minutes, the crowd handles the next thirty-five.
Watch the free throws tonight. {us} has left too many points at the line, and the bay is getting impatient.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. The causeway home is going to feel like a parade route.
Road win, and a tough one. {us} took the crowd's best and gave back a little better.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. Long drive home, but the bay will be waiting, and so will practice.
{them} held home court. The rematch comes to {town}, and we'll make sure they feel the humidity.

southern-miss.lean: Hub City quick and sharp-tongued; a runner who measures effort in Longleaf Trace miles and has no patience for anyone walking back on defense.

win: {us} by {margin}. That's Hub City basketball: everything runs through here, including the opponent, repeatedly.
Good win in {town}. The Golden Eagles played like they'd trained on the Longleaf Trace, and maybe they should.
loss: {us} lost at home and walked back on defense twice. I counted. I will always count.
Rough night. Lace up, run it off, and come back hungry. That's the whole speech.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. Tell the bay we said hello, and that the pines are doing just fine.
{them} came up from the coast for some pine air and left with a lesson. Golden Eagles, all night.
rival_loss: {rival} gets this one. I'll run an extra mile tomorrow and think about defensive rotations the whole way.
Lost to {rival}. The coast wins this round; the Hub City keeps the receipts and the rematch.
upset: Nobody picked {us}. That's fine. Golden Eagles don't read the forecast; they fly anyway.
Upset win for {us}! Somebody check on everybody who said otherwise. Gently, but do check.
preview: {them} visits {town}. My hunch: if {us} runs, {them} wilts by the second half. Pine country is humid.
Watch transition defense. If {us} sprints back every time, I'll have nothing to complain about, and I'd love that.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. Long bus ride, short memory, big smile.
Road win, and a gritty one. {us} kept running when the crowd tried to slow them down.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. The legs looked heavy. Good news: legs are trainable.
{them} held home court. The rematch is in {town}, and our gym knows exactly what to do with visitors.

troy.lean: Shameless Trojans man who'd trade a conference title for a good halftime band, forecasts every game wrong, and announces it with total confidence.

win: Trojans by {margin}! I called it, according to me, though the preview I wrote says otherwise. Ignore the preview.
Good win in {town}. I clapped so hard I lost my cap, and a kind lady in row C returned it with a lecture.
loss: {us} lost. I stared at the scoreboard so long the custodian asked if I needed a ride home.
Rough night at home. I'll be on the square tomorrow with boiled peanuts, telling anyone who'll listen it wasn't our fault.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}! I'll be wearing the belt around the square all week. Figuratively. I don't have the belt.
{them} came up from the coast and met a whole town that does not care for visitors. Politely, of course.
rival_loss: Lost to {rival}. My forecast for the week: grumpy, with a chance of more grumpy.
{rival} wins. I'm told I should be gracious. I'm told a lot of things. I'll try this one.
upset: Nobody picked {us}, including me, in writing, in print, which I'd like everyone to please forget.
Upset win! I yelled so loud the band looked back at me, and the band does not look back for anybody.
preview: {them} visits {town}. My hunch is the Trojans, and my hunches are right about as often as my umbrella.
I studied {them} closely this week. Fine team. Nice colors. That's all I've got, honestly.
road_win: {us} wins on the road! I listened in the truck and honked at a cow, who was unbothered.
Road win by {margin}. Proud of them. I'd go meet the bus, but I'm not sure which bus.
road_loss: Road loss. I'd blame the officiating, but I wasn't watching closely enough to say that honestly.
{them} held home court. Our band would've helped. Our band always helps. Bring the band next time.

ul-monroe.lean: Ouachita-calm and quick on the draw; roots for the Warhawks with a river guide's patience and a scout's red pen.

win: {us} by {margin}. The Ouachita kept rolling, and so did the Warhawks. Nice night on the river.
Good win in {town}. Patient offense, sharp defense, and {them} looking for a paddle by halftime.
loss: {us} lost at home. The shots were fine; the shot selection wasn't. There's a difference, and it's fixable.
{them} earned this one. {us} has a week to get its feet back under it.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. Neighbors are lovely, especially when they drive home quiet.
{them} came down the interstate expecting a party. We hosted graciously and kept the win.
rival_loss: {rival} gets this one. Neighbors win sometimes; you smile at them at the gas station and remember.
Lost to {rival}. The river rises and falls, and the Warhawks will rise again before the rematch.
upset: Nobody picked {us}. That's fine; Warhawks hunt better without an audience of believers.
Upset win for {us}! Somebody tell the river, because the rest of {town} already knows.
preview: {them} visits {town}. My hunch: {us} wins the pace battle, and the pace wins the night.
Watch the first media timeout. If {us} is even or better by then, I like where this is going.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. Nice and quiet, the way a Warhawk likes to hunt.
Road win, grown and steady. {us} took the punches and kept its shape.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. Nothing to panic about, plenty to fix. Back on the river Monday.
{them} held home court. The rematch is in {town}, where the river is ours.

brown.lean: Grades the Bears like a beloved seminar, wanders into tangents mid-recap, and now and then forgets to mention who won.

win: {us} by {margin}, which reminds me of a lecture I once gave on the quahog, though I can't quite recall why.
Class is in session, and {them} failed the quiz. I'd grade on a curve, but the curve also lost.
loss: {us} lost, and I've assigned myself a five-page reflection on why. I'm on page nine and haven't reached the game.
A disappointing evening in {town}. I loosened my cravat in search of comfort and found none.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. I'd prepared a tangent on the history of New Hampshire, but they've suffered enough.
{them} came down from the woods to learn a lesson. Class dismissed, and do read the syllabus next time.
rival_loss: Lost to {rival}. Office hours are canceled. I'll be on Thayer Street, muttering at a coffee.
{rival} wins this one. A footnote, I insist, in a very long book, which I'll be rereading by the fire.
upset: Nobody expected {us} to win, least of all the professor, who had already written the lecture on dignified defeat.
An upset! I'd explain it, but I've wandered into the history of the smoking jacket. Short version: we won.
preview: {them} visits {town} tonight. My hunch is {us}, though I warn you my hunches tend to run long.
Bears, class is in session. Tonight's reading: defend the arc. There will be a quiz, and it starts at tip.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. I celebrated by getting lost on the way to the bus, as is tradition.
A road win, and a scholarly one. I've marked it with a gold star and an entirely unnecessary footnote.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. I'd analyze it, but I've begun a tangent about the bus upholstery and can't stop.
{them} defended their home floor. Ever true, we'll see them in {town}, where the lecture hall favors us.

columbia.lean: Reviews every Lions game like an opening night: generous to a great second act, merciless to a lazy curtain call.

win: {us} by {margin}. A standing ovation from Morningside Heights, and I do not stand for just anyone.
A triumph in {town}. Crisp choreography, a strong second act, and {them} never once found their mark.
loss: {us} lost, and I'll call it an off night in previews. The critics, meaning me, expect revisions by the next show.
A disappointing evening. Even the 1 train home felt like a slow, sad overture.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. Do send our regards to Ithaca and its gorges; they'll need cheering up.
{them} came down from upstate for a night on the town. They got a matinee, and a short one.
rival_loss: {rival} takes this one. Upstate gets its applause tonight; we take back the stage at the rematch.
Lost to {rival}. I'll be reading the reviews on the 1 train and pretending not to.
upset: Nobody gave {us} a part in this show. The Lions rewrote the script and took the lead.
An upset, darling, and a stylish one. {us} stole the show from a cast that thought it owned the theater.
preview: {them} arrives in {town} tonight. My hunch: if {us} owns the opening number, the rest writes itself.
Lions, good evening. Tonight's role for {us}: patient, poised, and unwilling to be upstaged at home.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. A touring company outshining the local cast. Bravo.
Road win, beautifully staged. {us} took a hostile house and made it applaud, in its heart at least.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. Out-of-town tryouts are for finding flaws, and we found several.
{them} held serve at home. Fine. The rematch plays {town}, and our house does not do polite applause.

cornell.lean: Snow-practical and cheerfully exact; grades Big Red wins in inches of snowfall and has no time for teams that won't box out.

win: {us} by {margin}. Ithaca is gorges tonight, and so was that ball movement.
Good win in {town}. Shovel the walk, warm up the car, and enjoy a Big Red defense that never let up.
loss: {us} lost at home. Some nights the lake effect hits the shooting too. Dig out and try again.
{them} earned it. {us} didn't box out, and you can't win upstate without boxing out. It's practically state law.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. The city can keep its lights; we'll keep the waterfalls and the win.
{them} came up from Manhattan for some fresh air. We gave them plenty of that, and not much else.
rival_loss: {rival} gets this one. The city is loud, the drive is long, and we'll be ready for the rematch.
Lost to {rival}. I'll be sulking on a gorge trail in good boots, which is the upstate way.
upset: Nobody picked {us}. That's all right; nobody picks the snow either, and it shows up every year.
Upset win! Far above the forecasts and far above Cayuga. What a night to be Big Red.
preview: {them} comes to {town}. My hunch: rebounds decide it, and {us} boxes out like it's shoveling a driveway.
Big Red, the forecast is clear: defend the arc, win the glass, and bring a warm hat for the walk home.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. Long drive home on a very happy tank of gas.
Road win, practical and tidy. {us} did the work, took the win, and skipped the fuss.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. Nothing a long drive and a good film session can't fix.
{them} held home court. The rematch is in {town}, where visitors learn about real winter.

dartmouth.lean: Ski-lodge bright and trail-tough; cheers the Big Green like a powder day and expects them to climb the hard pitches without complaint.

win: {us} by {margin}! Greetings from Hanover, where that felt like first chair on a powder morning.
Great win in {town}. Clean edges, strong legs, and {them} never found the trail.
loss: {us} lost at home. Wax the skis, check the bindings, and get back on the lift tomorrow.
A rough run tonight. {them} earned it, and {us} has a long climb ahead. Good thing we like climbing.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. Providence can keep its fancy jackets; we'll keep the win and the wool socks.
{them} came north for some fresh air, and the North Country gave them plenty. Stay green!
rival_loss: {rival} gets this one. Fine. I'll take a long walk along the river and plot the rematch.
Lost to {rival}. Pack it in, warm up by the fire, and get back on the trail Monday.
upset: Nobody picked {us}. Up here, we don't wait for permission to climb a mountain.
Upset win! I'd ring the cowbell if I hadn't lost it in the excitement. Big Green, everybody!
preview: {them} comes to {town}. My hunch: {us} sets the pace early and makes them chase all night.
Big Green, conditions are good: defend hard, share the ball, and dress in layers for the drive home.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. Good legs travel. Stay green!
Road win, and a gutsy one. {us} climbed out of a hole and finished strong at the summit.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. Some trails are harder away from home, and we'll know this one next time.
{them} held home court. The rematch is in {town}, and our hill is steeper than theirs.

harvard.lean: Covers the Crimson like a closing argument: crisp, evidence-based, and quietly certain she has already won the room.

win: {us} by {margin}. Motion carried, objection overruled, and the floor remains mine.
A decisive win in {town}. {them} brought arguments; the Crimson brought evidence.
loss: {us} lost at home. I concede the point, under protest, with a rebuttal already drafted for the next game.
{them} made the better case tonight. {us} has a week to prepare a stronger one, and it had better be.
rival_win: Beat {rival} by {margin}. The debate is settled until next time, and the transcript will be framed.
{them} came up from New Haven with talking points. The Crimson came with a closing argument.
rival_loss: {rival} wins this round. I'll be filing an appeal, by which I mean a rematch, and I intend to win it.
Lost to {rival}. I've reviewed the tape and find the verdict technically correct and personally unacceptable.
upset: Nobody gave {us} a chance? An unusual position for us, and I must say the Crimson argued it beautifully.
Upset win. The underdog makes the best closing argument, and tonight {us} had the last word.
preview: {them} visits {town}. My thesis: {us} wins the turnover battle, and the rest follows as a matter of logic.
Crimson, the floor is yours tonight. Opening statement: defend the arc. Closing statement: make your free throws.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}. Away venue, home result. The record will reflect it.
Road win, argued well. {us} let the crowd make its noise and then made its case anyway.
road_loss: {us} lost on the road. A setback, not a verdict. Prepare the rebuttal.
{them} held home court. Noted for the record. The rematch convenes in {town}.

penn.lean: Writes every Quakers win like a founding document and every loss like a clerical error; drafts his proclamations a half beat after the crowd has gone home.
penn.pet: the Palestra as the cathedral of the sport

win: Let it be entered into the record, in my finest hand, that {us} prevailed by {margin}; I would have read it aloud, but the Palestra had already emptied.
Hear ye: {us} by {margin}, and I have sharpened a fresh quill solely to underline it twice.
loss: A setback, duly noted, and I shall blame the ink, the lighting, and the draft from the east doors before I blame a single Quaker.
The Palestra has seen worse nights than this one, and I have personally written lengthy, unpublished letters about most of them.
rival_win: {rival} has been defeated, and I have composed a proclamation of seven paragraphs, which my editor has kindly trimmed to this sentence.
Tigers came to Philadelphia and left in a stripe of humility; I rang a small hand bell in the press row and was asked to stop.
rival_loss: I decline to discuss {rival} further, and I have so informed my quill, which agrees.
A grievous evening; I drafted a formal complaint to the rims, and the rims, as usual, did not reply.
upset: Nobody gave {us} a chance against {them}, which I would have mentioned in advance had I finished my preview before tipoff.
Strike the odds from the record; {us} upended {them}, and I have misplaced my wig in the excitement.
preview: Hear ye: I expect {us} to honor the Palestra tonight, though I have been wrong before and documented it at length.
Mark me, {them} has never truly understood the old building, and the old building remembers that sort of thing.
road_win: {us} carried the day abroad by {margin}, and I have already begun my letter home, though the bus beat me back.
A road victory over {them}, earned in a strange gym among strangers, which is precisely how the colonies did it, or so I tell myself.
road_loss: The journey home shall be long and the turnpike longer; I have composed a lament in the margins of my program.
Away gyms lack the Palestra's dignity, and tonight {us} played as though it noticed.

princeton.lean: Treats every Tigers game like a black-tie soiree he is hosting, and every backdoor cut like a guest arriving in the perfect outfit; somehow never quite catches which room the party moved to.

win: {us} by {margin} in Jadwin, darlings, and I'd have toasted the backdoor cut if I hadn't been in the wrong hallway with the canapes.
A {margin}-point evening, beautifully passed and sharply dressed; I believe I applauded the opening tip by accident.
loss: Not every party lands, and tonight the music was off; I'll be reviewing the guest list, which is to say the shot chart.
{them} crashed the soiree and stayed past midnight, and frankly I was the last to notice they had arrived.
rival_win: Penn came up the turnpike in its Sunday best and left with the check; I wore the stripes for exactly this occasion.
Beating {rival} is the one invitation I never decline, and tonight it came with dessert.
rival_loss: {rival} wins one, and I shall smile through it like a host whose ice sculpture has just melted on camera.
A rough night against {rival}; I spent the second half insisting the scoreboard was a decorative piece.
upset: Nobody RSVP'd to {us} upsetting {them}, so naturally it became the party of the season and I arrived fashionably late.
An upset over {them}, and I'm told I was very charming about it, although I was mostly confused.
preview: Expect cuts, expect patience, and expect me to mispronounce the {them} mascot with total confidence.
My hunch: {us} keeps the tempo elegant and lets {them} grow restless before the cheese course.
road_win: {us} took the party on the road and won by {margin}, which proves good manners travel even when I forget my bag.
A road win at {them}, smooth and unhurried; I tipped the bus driver twice out of sheer relief.
road_loss: Away from Jadwin the lighting is unkind, and tonight so was the rim; we'll host better next time.
{them} threw the better party tonight, and I'm not too proud to admit I stayed for the snacks.

yale.lean: Covers Yale from a leather armchair, forgives the Bulldogs nearly anything, and is perpetually two plays behind because he was refilling the decanter.

win: {us} by {margin}, I gather, and I raised a glass at what I'm told was the correct moment, roughly.
A pleasant evening in {town}; the Bulldogs moved the ball briskly and I managed nearly all of it from my chair.
loss: A disappointing result, though the sherry was excellent, and I shall be writing to the committee about one of those things.
{them} played admirably, I suppose, in the way one admires weather from indoors.
rival_win: {rival} has been dispatched, and the club is buying, which is to say I have been told I am buying.
Beating {rival} restores the natural order of things, a phrase I use about once a year and mean every time.
rival_loss: One does not discuss losing to {rival} at the club; I shall simply sit very quietly and recolor slightly.
{rival} won, and I have removed the striped tie for the evening as a gesture of mourning and mild sulking.
upset: An upset over {them}, and I confess I learned of it from a waiter who was clearly paying closer attention.
Nobody fancied {us} tonight, myself included, as I had already asked for my coat.
preview: A hunch from the armchair: {us} grinds it out, and I nod off pleasantly during the second media timeout.
{them} arrives with something to prove; the Bulldogs arrive with something to defend, and I arrive with a cushion.
road_win: A road win at {them} by {margin}; I listened from the club and I'm told my cheering frightened the portraits.
Victory on foreign soil, and the drive home up the shoreline will be all the more agreeable for it.
road_loss: Away games are tiresome, and tonight was especially so, though I hear the {them} hot chocolate was decent.
The Bulldogs fell on the road, and I have retreated to the library, where nobody keeps score.

campbell.lean: Calls it straight and plain, gives the other bench its due, and saves his real warmth for the Camels who rebound hard and the folks who drove the back roads in to watch.

win: {us} by {margin}, and I'd point you to the glass, because the Camels owned every loose ball that mattered.
Good home win in Buies Creek; folks drove a long way on two-lane roads to see that, and it was worth the gas.
loss: {them} earned it, plain and simple, and {us} will find out on the film how many boards walked away.
Tough night at home; you don't lose the rebounding fight in your own gym and expect to keep the game.
rival_win: {rival} came down from the Piedmont and went home quiet; that one will keep folks warm until spring.
Beating {rival} feels good in Buies Creek, and I'll admit I let my voice go up a half step for it.
rival_loss: Credit to {rival}, who were tougher on the glass tonight; the Camels will remember that, and so will I.
I don't love saying it, but {rival} played the cleaner game, and that's the honest report.
upset: Nobody outside Harnett County circled this one, but {us} beat {them} on effort, and effort travels.
An upset over {them}, earned the old way: block out, go get it, and don't apologize.
preview: Watch the glass tonight; whoever wins the second chances between {us} and {them} probably wins the evening.
{them} has the bigger name, but names don't rebound, and I like the Camels to make it a fight.
road_win: {us} wins on the road by {margin}, and the long ride home just got a whole lot shorter.
A road win at {them} built on toughness, which is about the most Buies Creek thing a team can do.
road_loss: {us} came up short on the road, and the box score tells you where: second chances, again.
Hard place to play, and {them} made it harder; the Camels will be better for the bus ride.

charleston.lean: Gracious to every guest and merciless about their manners; she roots for the Cougars like it's a family obligation and runs the room like she owns the house.
charleston.pet: Lowcountry hospitality, and who abuses it

win: {us} by {margin}, and we sent {them} home with a full belly and a polite little lesson.
A lovely evening in the Holy City: the Cougars ran, the crowd sang, and I never once had to raise my voice.
loss: Our guests forgot their manners and remembered their jump shots, and I will be noting both in the guestbook.
A rare loss at home, and I'll grant {them} a gracious nod before I go reorganize the whole defense in my head.
rival_win: {rival} came down the coast feeling bold and drove back up it with a little less to say.
Beating {rival} is how I like my evenings, warm, a bit humid, and decided well before the last call.
rival_loss: Bless {rival}'s heart, they played well, and I will say so exactly once.
We lost to {rival}, and I'll be keeping my seersucker in the closet until I've properly forgiven everyone.
upset: Nobody expected {us} to handle {them}, which tells me nobody's been paying attention to this town.
An upset, they'll call it, though I'd call it {them} finally being shown proper Charleston hospitality.
preview: {them} visits tonight, and I expect us to be charming right up until the opening tip.
My hunch: {us} runs early, and {them} spends the second half fanning itself on the bench.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and I trust our hosts will remember us fondly, or at least clearly.
{us} went visiting and came home with the silverware, so to speak, and nobody had to be rude about it.
road_loss: Away games are someone else's party, and tonight {them} set the menu; we'll host the rematch.
{us} lost on the road, and I'll be reminding them that a long drive is no excuse for sloppy footwork.

drexel.lean: Thinks every Drexel possession is a heist he personally planned, and is genuinely surprised when the Dragons improvise something better than his scheme.
drexel.pet: half-court angles and the perfect screen

win: {us} by {margin}, and I called the whole thing in my notebook, except for every part that actually happened.
Dragons win at home, and the lair was loud enough that I lost my train of thought for a delightful twenty minutes.
loss: {them} found every angle I was going to point out, which, honestly, feels a little personal.
Bad night in the lair; I'm going to redraw my whiteboard and pretend this didn't happen to my brilliant theories.
rival_win: {rival} brought the claws, but the Dragons brought the fire, and I brought a diagram nobody asked to see.
Beating {rival} never gets old, and I have already texted my landlord about it, which he did not need.
rival_loss: {rival} got us tonight, and I'm taking it harder than the team, which they'll tell you is very on brand for me.
I had a plan to beat {rival}; unfortunately the plan lived in my notebook and not on the floor.
upset: Upset over {them}, and I'd love to say I saw it coming, but I was busy predicting the exact opposite.
Nobody picked {us} over {them}, and for once I'm glad nobody listened to me either.
preview: Look for the angles tonight; I've got three theories about {them}, and at least one is probably right.
My hunch: {us} screens {them} into confusion, and I get to act like I knew it all along.
road_win: {us} wins away by {margin}, and the ride back down I-95 is going to be all angles and big talk, mostly mine.
A road win at {them}, which I'll be claiming as my idea for at least the next week.
road_loss: {them} out-schemed us on their floor, and I'm a little impressed, which I'll deny on air.
Road losses sting in Philadelphia, and this one stung me right in the whiteboard.

elon.lean: Believes every Phoenix deficit is just the setup for a rise, narrates comebacks before they happen, and is right just often enough to be dangerous.

win: {us} by {margin}, and the Phoenix rose right on schedule, which is to say whenever I asked it to.
Rise and shine, {town}: a home win, bright and fiery, and I'm not coming down for a while.
loss: Ashes tonight, sure, but I've read this story before and I know how the next chapter goes.
{them} burned brighter at the end; we'll take the smoke, study it, and come back hotter.
rival_win: {rival} came up from Buies Creek and got scorched; I'd say I'm sorry, but I'm on the air.
Beating {rival} is my favorite kind of fire, the kind that warms the whole Piedmont.
rival_loss: {rival} wins one, and I'll grant them the evening, but phoenixes are famously bad at staying down.
A loss to {rival} stings, and I'm putting it right on the list of things we rise from.
upset: Nobody saw {us} beating {them} except me, and I've been saying it in this cape for weeks.
Upset over {them}, and if you'd asked me at halftime, I'd have told you, calmly, to watch.
preview: Down early is fine; {us} plays its best basketball when everybody else is ready to leave.
My hunch on {them}: a tight first half, then the Phoenix rises, because that's simply what it does.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and we lit up somebody else's building, which is the best kind of fire.
{us} rose on the road at {them}, and I can feel the cape fluttering from here.
road_loss: {them} held us down tonight on their floor, and I respect it, and I'll see them in the rematch.
A road loss, a long drive home, and a team that I promise will rise again before the weekend.

hampton.lean: Runs coverage like a ship's log: crisp, proud, unimpressed by sloppy ball handling, and fiercely loyal to the Pirates when they play disciplined.

win: {us} by {margin}, and the log will show a crew that took care of the ball from stem to stern.
Home win by the sea; the Pirates played in step, and I don't ask for anything more than that.
loss: {them} took this one, and the log will show too many turnovers; we'll drill it until it doesn't.
A loss at home, and I'll put it plainly: the Pirates got loose with the ball and paid for it.
rival_win: {rival} came up the road with a band and a plan, and the Pirates sent both home quiet.
Beating {rival} is a proud night on the water, and I'm logging it in ink.
rival_loss: Respect to {rival}, who played the cleaner game; the Pirates will report back ready.
{rival} won the battle tonight, and I'll be reviewing every possession until I'm satisfied.
upset: An upset over {them}, earned with discipline, and I expect every hand on deck to stay humble.
Nobody charted a course for {us} beating {them}, so the Pirates charted their own.
preview: Watch the ball security tonight; whichever crew wastes fewer possessions sails home with this one.
{them} likes to speed the game up, and I like the Pirates to keep a steady hand on the wheel.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and the crew kept its composure in hostile water; that's the standard.
{us} handled {them} on the road, and I'm proud of every disciplined possession of it.
road_loss: Rough seas on the road tonight; the Pirates will regroup, and so will I.
{them} had the home crowd and the better night, and the log will say so honestly.

hofstra.lean: Covers every Pride game like it's his own family's Sunday dinner, roots without shame, and keeps mixing up basketball terms with the specials board.
hofstra.pet: the deli order as a game plan

win: {us} by {margin}, and I'm buying everybody a sandwich, metaphorically, because I left my wallet at the counter.
That was a full meal in Hempstead, appetizer to cannoli, and I want seconds already.
loss: We lost at home, and I'm not saying the kitchen was closed, I'm saying somebody forgot to turn on the stove.
{them} came in hungry and we served it up for 'em; I'm gonna need a minute and a pickle.
rival_win: {rival} comes in from the north shore and leaves with a doggie bag; I'm sorry, I'm not sorry.
Beating {rival} is my favorite dish on the menu, and I tried to order it twice tonight.
rival_loss: {rival} got us, and I'm too upset to eat, which if you know me is a five-alarm emergency.
Losing to {rival} is like dropping the sandwich on the way to the car; I'm still staring at the pavement.
upset: Nobody gave {us} a shot against {them}, and now I'm the guy saying I knew it, with mustard on my tie.
An upset over {them}, and Hempstead is going to celebrate like the bagels just came out of the oven.
preview: My hunch tonight: {us} comes out hungry, and I tell you that every night, and some nights I'm right.
{them} is a tough order, but this team knows what it wants and it's not leaving without dessert.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and I'm already planning what to eat on the Expressway home.
{us} beat {them} on their floor, and I'm telling you, that's takeout that tastes better than home cooking.
road_loss: A road loss, and the traffic home is gonna feel twice as long, plus I forgot snacks.
{them} had the home cooking tonight; we'll get 'em back on the Island, where I know the menu.

monmouth.lean: Shameless Hawks booster with a boardwalk swagger, talks smack like she's running a ring toss, and counts every Parkway exit on the way to a road game.

win: {us} by {margin}, and the Shore is loud tonight; somebody open the windows on the boardwalk.
Home win in West Long Branch, and I'd call that a straight-up jackpot on the ring toss.
loss: {them} got lucky on our floor, and I'm saying that with my whole chest, and I'll say it Monday too.
A home loss, and I'm grumpier than a Saturday in July on the Parkway southbound.
rival_win: {rival} took the ferry of shame home tonight, and I'm not even sorry about the ferry.
Beating {rival} is my favorite summer in winter, sun's out, sand's warm, Hawks are flying.
rival_loss: {rival} won, fine, and I'm going to sit in my car on the Parkway and think about it.
I'm not talking about {rival} tonight; ask me after a slice and a walk on the boards.
upset: Nobody thought {us} could take {them}, and the Jersey Shore is telling you, loud, they were wrong.
An upset over {them}, and I'm doing a little boardwalk victory lap right here at the desk.
preview: {them} is coming to the Shore, and I hope they packed for weather, because the Hawks bring it.
My hunch: {us} flies early and {them} spends all night chasing it like a gull after fries.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and every Parkway exit home is going to feel like a parade route.
{us} went into {them}'s house and turned the lights off on the way out; love that for us.
road_loss: A road loss and a long ride up the Turnpike; I'm counting exits and grudges, in that order.
{them} had the crowd tonight, but the Hawks will have the boardwalk when we see 'em again.

nc-at.lean: Calls the Aggies like she's leading the band onto the field, every possession in rhythm, and gives proud, measured credit to anyone who can keep step.

win: {us} by {margin}, in step and on beat, and Greensboro is marching home happy tonight.
Home win, the band was loud, the Aggies were louder, and I barely needed my microphone.
loss: {them} broke our rhythm tonight, and that's on us to find the beat again by Saturday.
A home loss stings, but this program has marched through tougher stretches with its head up.
rival_win: {rival} came down from the coast and couldn't keep time with us; Aggie Pride, all night long.
Beating {rival} is the best halftime show I know, and tonight it ran all forty minutes.
rival_loss: Credit to {rival}, they kept the better rhythm tonight; we'll tune up and see them again.
A loss to {rival} hurts, and I'll let the drums carry that one for me.
upset: Nobody expected {us} over {them}, and that's fine; the Aggies march to their own count.
An upset over {them}, and Greensboro is dancing in the stands with the band right behind them.
preview: Tempo tonight is everything; if {us} sets the beat early, {them} will be playing catch-up all evening.
Watch the pace and listen to the band; when both are rolling, the Aggies are hard to stop.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and we brought our own rhythm into somebody else's house.
{us} kept perfect time at {them}, and that's a long, proud bus ride home to Greensboro.
road_loss: A road loss, and {them} set the tempo; the Aggies will find their step again soon.
{them} played sharp on their floor, and I'll give them that, briskly, and move on.

northeastern.lean: Fast-talking Huskies loyalist who covers the team like a co-op job she's acing, knows every Green Line delay, and has no patience for a lazy closeout.
northeastern.pet: the Green Line and the co-op grind

win: {us} by {margin}, wicked good, and the Huskies did the work faster than the Green Line ever has.
Home win on Huntington, and that's the kind of hustle this whole city runs on.
loss: {them} took one in our building, and I'm not mad, I'm just writing down every lazy closeout.
A home loss, and the T ride back is gonna feel extra long tonight, which is saying something.
rival_win: {rival} came up from the Island and went home with nothin'; that's a good night on Huntington.
Beating {rival} feels like getting a seat on the train at rush hour; rare and completely deserved.
rival_loss: {rival} got us tonight, and I'm putting it in the file marked we'll see you in March.
Losing to {rival} is a cold walk up Huntington in February, and I've made that walk plenty.
upset: Nobody thought {us} had this against {them}, but this city loves a team that clocks in early.
An upset over {them}, and somewhere on the Green Line, a whole car just cheered.
preview: Watch the closeouts tonight; if the Huskies hustle the way they're supposed to, {them} is in trouble.
My hunch: {us} grinds {them} down like a winter commute, slow, cold, and totally worth it.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and the Huskies traveled light and played heavy; love to see it.
{us} won at {them}, and that's a co-op performance review I'd frame.
road_loss: A road loss, and the trip home is long, but this team's been through Boston winters, they'll be fine.
{them} played better on their floor tonight; we'll get the rematch on ours.

stony-brook.lean: Easygoing old salt who gives the other side a fair wind, reads every game like a tide chart, and is usually the last aboard when the momentum shifts.
stony-brook.pet: tides, weather and the ferry schedule

win: {us} by {margin}, a fair wind and a following sea, and I only checked the tide chart twice.
Home win at the Brook, and I'd tell you exactly when it turned, but I was still looking at the weather.
loss: {them} sailed better tonight, plain as a lighthouse, and the Seawolves will trim the sails.
A home loss, and I'm blaming the tide, which has never once listened to my complaints.
rival_win: {rival} came out from Hempstead and found the Sound a bit choppier than they expected.
Beating {rival} is a calm harbor at sunset, and I'm going to sit here and enjoy the view.
rival_loss: {rival} had the better wind tonight, and I'll admit it, even if I grumble about it on the dock.
Lost to {rival}; I'm going to go stare at the water a while, which fixes most things.
upset: Nobody charted {us} beating {them}, including me, and I chart everything, mostly incorrectly.
An upset over {them}, and I'm told the momentum shifted around halftime; I'll take their word for it.
preview: Steady on tonight; {us} plays best with a patient hand on the tiller, and {them} likes rough water.
My hunch is a close one, and I've packed a thermos for a long evening at the Brook.
road_win: A road win by {margin}, and the Seawolves found calm water in a hostile harbor.
{us} won at {them}, and I'd say it was smooth sailing, but I missed the first ten minutes looking for parking.
road_loss: A road loss and a long drive back along the Sound; we'll catch the next tide.
{them} handled their home waters tonight, and fair play to them, honestly.

towson.lean: Fierce Tigers partisan with a grin full of teeth, treats every steal like a trophy, and has opinions about the York Road traffic she will share during timeouts.

win: {us} by {margin}, and that was a tiger playing with its food; I enjoyed every bite.
Home win in Towson, the press was suffocating, and the roar in that building is still ringing.
loss: {them} slipped our press tonight; enjoy it, because that doesn't happen twice.
A home loss, and I am pacing the cage about it; nobody come near the desk.
rival_win: {rival} came down from Philly breathing fire and left with smoke and a lot of turnovers.
Beating {rival} is my favorite meal of the season, and the steals were the seasoning.
rival_loss: {rival} got us tonight, and I'm writing it on the wall in claw marks so nobody forgets.
A loss to {rival} is a bad night in the jungle, and I'll be loud about the rematch.
upset: Nobody gave {us} a chance against {them}, which is exactly when tigers do their best hunting.
